case_name: Gurnek Singh and Another v State of Punjab
respondent:
State of Punjab
Supreme Court of India

27 September 1988
Cr.A. No. 444 of 1978
The Judgment was delivered by: THAKKAR, J.
1. The trial court held, and the High Court concurred, that appellants were the culprits who had fired at and injured Gurdarshan Singh (who succumbed to his injuries) as also his father, brother and mother (injured eye-witnesses PWs. 8, 9 and 10). The appellants have assailed the said finding and the order of conviction and sentence for the murder of Gurdarshan Singh and the attempt to commit the murder of PWs. 8, 9 and 10. For the former offence appellants are convicted under S. 302 read with S. 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and sentenced to imprisonment for life. For the latter they have been convicted under S. 307 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 4 years.
2. The occurrence took place on October 13, 1972 at about 7.00 p.m. near the haveli of the victims and near the house of appellant
facts: The trial court held, and the High Court concurred, that appellants were the culprits who had fired at and injured Gurdarshan Singh (who succumbed to his injuries) as also his father, brother and mother (injured eye-witnesses PWs.8, 9 and 10).
The occurrence took place on October 13, 1972 at about 7.00 p.m. near the haveli of the victims and near the house of appellant No.1 Gurnek Singh which adjoins the said haveli.
The evidence relied upon by the prosecution in order to establish the guilt of the appellants consisted of: ...
The occurrence took place on October 13, 1972 at about 7.00 p.m. near the haveli of the victims and near the house of appellant No.1 Gurnek Singh which adjoins the said haveli.
Appellant No.1 had demanded plot No.111, admeasuring 19 marlas which had fallen to the share of P.W.8 (father of the deceased) which demand had not been acceded to by PW 8.
The trial court did not consider the evidence as regards, motive reliable.
The High Court, on the other hand, came to the conclusion that the evidence regarding motive was satisfactory and that the trial court was not justified in rejecting this evidence.
issues: Whether the appellants were the culprits who had fired at and injured Gurdarshan Singh (who succumbed to his injuries) as also his father, brother and mother (injured eye-witnesses PWs.8, 9 and 10)?
Whether the evidence regarding motive was reliable?
Whether the evidence regarding dying declaration was reliable?
Whether the evidence regarding recovery of weapons was reliable?
Whether the delay in lodging FIR was reasonable?
petitioner_arguments: The appellants have assailed the said finding and the order of conviction and sentence for the murder of Gurdarshan Singh and the attempt to commit the murder of PWs.8, 9 and 10.
Learned counsel for the appellants has contended that the following circumstances have not been accorded due weight by the High Court: ...
The fire-arms which have been recovered were not shown to have been used in the commission of the crime;
There was a delay in lodging of the FIR;
The medical evidence rendered the prosecution version suspect.
respondent_arguments: The trial court held, and the High Court concurred, that appellants were the culprits who had fired at and injured Gurdarshan Singh (who succumbed to his injuries) as also his father, brother and mother (injured eye-witnesses PWs.8, 9 and 10).
The evidence regarding motive was satisfactory and that the trial court was not justified in rejecting this evidence.
The evidence of the injured eye-witnesses is considered reliable, trustworthy, and safe to act upon.
court_reasoning: We have carefully scrutinized the evidence of the three injured eye-witnesses. We are of the opinion that the trial court and the High Court were right in accepting their evidence.

The presence of these three witnesses at the time of occurrence is beyond question having regard to the fact that all the three of them have sustained injuries by pellets on account of the gun-shots fired at them in the course of the very same transaction at the very time and place of occurrence.
We see no reason to differ from the concurrent finding recorded in this behalf.
The evidence regarding absconding which both the courts have accepted and which is adequate and satisfactory lends further credence to the prosecution case.
holding: The appeal, therefore, fails and is dismissed. The appellants shall surrender to custody in order to undergo the remaining part of the sentence.
